newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH OFFICERS AT EASE OVER BOGUS GENERAL'S VISIT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH OFFICERS AT EASE OVER BOGUS GENERAL'S VISIT.

text.p: Czech officers and conscripts snapped to attention for a general's surprise inspection, only later to find he was a defence ministry warehouse worker on holiday who requisitioned a brassy surplus uniform for himself.

The daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Friday quoted Major Miroslav Meleg, commander at the Boletice training base, as saying a uniformed man arrived, announced himself as a lieutenant general, and was afforded full honours of an official visit.
Major Meleg said he personally received the bogus general, customarily yelling out his name and rank while saluting, as did other soldiers who encountered him on the base.
"It was strange to me, that a general didn't wear a hat and had only a civilian coat draped over his uniform," Meleg said.
The "general" and Meleg discussed problems in the defence ministry, then the major led his superior on a base inspection.
"From the beginning it seemed to me something wasn't right, but he produced a pass from the defence ministry and had good knowledge of the field," Major Meleg said.
While the bogus general took a toilet break, Meleg called Prague and was told that the man's name was indeed in the ministry data base, but without the abbreviated rank of "gen".
After the "general" left, Meleg checked with colleagues who knew nothing of him. Returning to his ministry job, the imposter was greeted by police and charged with a misdemeanour.
The 47-year-old, who was not named, told the paper that he has yet to receive the fine request in the mail.
"It was a prank and I guess they took it that way," said the warehouse worker, who added that he just wanted to feel what it was like to be one of the bigwigs he saw every day.
